result.note: Sports policy story with a modest governance angle; tested the May 2026 bilateral-versus-multilateral rule, India's hosting bids and the 2026 T20 World Cup venue arrangement.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements in the context of India's sporting engagement with Pakistan as of May 2026:
items: A memo issued by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in May 2026 cleared the way for Pakistani teams to compete in multilateral events hosted by India.
Under the May 2026 policy, India will host Pakistan for standalone bilateral matches.
India is bidding to host the 2036 Olympics and the 2038 Asian Games.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because India will still refuse to play one-on-one series against Pakistan or host them for standalone matches; only multilateral events are opened up. India is also bidding for the 2030 Commonwealth Games, and TBB notes that alienating global sporting bodies would hurt its 2036 Olympic bid.
questions.source: India will still refuse to play one-on-one series against Pakistan or host them for standalone matches.

questions.prompt: During the India-hosted T20 World Cup in 2026, in which country did Pakistan play its matches?
questions.explain: Pakistan played its matches in Sri Lanka to avoid the optics of crossing the border. Bilateral cricket between India and Pakistan has been frozen since 2012, and a military skirmish in May 2025 hardened the freeze further.
questions.source: During this year’s India-hosted T20 World Cup, Pakistan played its matches in Sri Lanka to avoid the optics of crossing the border.
